mcqs.question: Which description best defines natural farming (Prakritik Kheti)?
options: Chemical-free farming based on on-farm biomass and local cattle-based inputs
Chemical farming based on purchased synthetic inputs
Seed treatment based only on lime and soil
Mulching based only on air–moisture balance
mcqs.explanation: Natural farming, or Prakritik Kheti, is chemical-free and relies on on-farm biomass and local cattle-based inputs. The option referring only to air–moisture balance describes Waaphasa, not the overall concept of natural farming.

mcqs.question: In natural farming, what does the practice of Waaphasa refer to?
options: Air–moisture balance in the root zone
A fermented microbial solution
Seed treatment
Mulching
mcqs.explanation: Waaphasa refers to maintaining the air–moisture balance in the root zone. A fermented microbial solution, seed treatment and mulching are separate natural-farming practices.

mcqs.question: Which policy combination is associated with reducing the use of chemical fertilisers by States?
options: National Mission on Natural Farming and PM-PRANAM
National Mission on Natural Farming alone
PM-PRANAM alone
National Mission on Natural Farming and no fertiliser-related policy
mcqs.explanation: The National Mission on Natural Farming and PM-PRANAM are associated with States cutting chemical fertiliser use. The other options incorrectly omit or alter this policy combination.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the fertiliser-policy lesson associated with Sri Lanka is incorrect?
options: A sudden fertiliser ban in Sri Lanka is cited as a lesson for policy discussions.
Sri Lanka's sudden fertiliser ban is regarded as a policy lesson.
The Sri Lankan fertiliser ban was sudden and is cited as a lesson.
Sri Lanka's gradual fertiliser ban is cited as a lesson for policy discussions.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes the ban from sudden to gradual. The relevant lesson concerns Sri Lanka's sudden fertiliser ban.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?

1. Natural farming clusters in March 2026 covered 8.80 lakh ha and 18.19 lakh farmers.
2. Per Drop More Crop had covered approximately 109 lakh ha by May 2026 and has operated since 2015–16.
3. Agriculture recorded decadal growth of 4.45% during FY16–FY25.
4. Per Drop More Crop had covered approximately 109 lakh ha by March 2026.
options: Only one
Only two
Only three
All four
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is Only three. Statement 4 is incorrect because the approximately 109 lakh ha figure for Per Drop More Crop is given for May 2026, not March 2026.

mcqs.question: Which combination correctly describes the Soil Health Cards scheme?
options: 25.89 crore generated; scheme from 2015; 12 parameters; issued every 2 years
25.89 crore generated; scheme from 2015; 12 parameters; issued annually
25.89 crore generated; scheme from 2015; issued without parameters; every 2 years
25.89 crore generated; scheme from 2015; 12 parameters; issued only once
mcqs.explanation: The Soil Health Cards scheme was started in 2015, has generated 25.89 crore cards, assesses 12 parameters and follows a 2-year cycle. The other options alter the frequency or the number of parameters.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding natural-farming and allied agricultural schemes.

List-I
(a) National Mission on Natural Farming
(b) PKVY
(c) Rainfed Area Development
(d) Agroforestry component under PM-RKVY

List-II
(i) 2015; organic farming
(ii) ₹4,000 per acre per year for 2 years, maximum 1 acre
(iii) Since 2014–15; approximately 20 ha clusters; ₹30,000 per family; ₹343.86 crore in 2025–26
(iv) ₹78.31 crore in 2025–26; 27 States; 176.59 lakh saplings
options: a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv
a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii
a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-i, c-iii and d-iv. NMNF provides ₹4,000 per acre per year for 2 years with a maximum of 1 acre; PKVY concerns organic farming; Rainfed Area Development and Agroforestry have the respective figures shown.

mcqs.question: Which set consists entirely of natural-farming inputs listed for the natural farming programme?
options: Beejamrut, Jeevamrut, GhanJeevamrut, Neemastra and Dashparni
Beejamrut, Jeevamrut, Soil Health Cards, Neemastra and Dashparni
Beejamrut, GhanJeevamrut, Per Drop More Crop, Neemastra and Dashparni
Jeevamrut, GhanJeevamrut, Neemastra, Dashparni and PM-PRANAM
mcqs.explanation: The listed natural-farming inputs are Beejamrut, Jeevamrut, GhanJeevamrut, Neemastra and Dashparni. Soil Health Cards, Per Drop More Crop and PM-PRANAM are not inputs in this list.

mcqs.question: Natural farming is linked with which Sustainable Development Goal and target?
options: SDG 13 and Target 13.1
SDG 13 without any target linkage
Target 13.1 without an SDG linkage
SDG 13 and Target 13.1 as separate, unrelated linkages
mcqs.explanation: The stated SDG linkage for natural farming is SDG 13, Target 13.1. The other options either omit one part of the linkage or incorrectly treat the two elements as unrelated.
